    AI Overview
    The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) is a real-time market index representing the market's expectation of 30-day forward-looking volatility of the S&P 500® Index (SPX), often referred to as Wall Street's "fear gauge". As of mid-April 2026, the VIX experienced a significant collapse, dropping to around 16–18 levels from higher, indicating decreased market panic. It is calculated using SPX option prices and generally has an inverse relationship with the S&P 500. 
    Key Aspects of the VIX: 
    • Purpose: Measures market risk and investor sentiment, with higher values indicating greater fear and volatility (often >30) and lower values (often <20) indicating stability.
    • Calculation: Uses a 30-day, constant, weighted measure of SPX options with Friday expirations.
    • Behavior: The VIX is mean-reverting, meaning it tends to return to its historical average rather than staying high or low permanently.
    • Trading: While you cannot buy the VIX directly, investors trade it through futures, options, and exchange-traded products (ETPs) to hedge against market declines. 
    Recent Performance (April 2026):
    Following a 44% crash in the three weeks ending April 17, 2026, the VIX hit a nine-week low of 16.87, signalling a shift toward lower volatility. History suggests this type of rapid drop in the VIX can be positive for equity market performance.

    People also ask
    What does a VIX of 22 mean?
    But the VIX's values—the numbers you see—express an expected annualized volatility. For example, if the VIX shows a reading of 22, that means that there is a 68% probability that the S&P 500 trades within a range of +/- 22% over the next year. ( The 68% probability represents one standard deviation.)Apr 22, 2025

    Is VIX bullish or bearish?
    The VIX is often referred to as the market's “fear index or fear gauge”. The performance of the VIX is inversely related to the S&P 500 – when the price of the VIX goes up, the price of the S&P 500 usually goes down. If the VIX is rising, demand for options is increasing, and therefore, becoming more expensive.

    Should I buy or sell when VIX is high?
    When there is a spike in the VIX, this means traders in the S&P 500 options market expect that market volatility will increase. The higher the VIX Index, the higher the fear, which, according to market contrarians, is considered a buy signal.
